_why: ADR 0075's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
Four claims on the landing page contradicted the code, and only one of
the four flattered the product. That is the finding: this is not a
check against exaggeration but against UNVERIFIED claims, which drift
in whichever direction the last edit went.
P5 is the row that escaped the original hand-run table. Every replay
used the exact casing found in the source, so making the match
case-sensitive was invisible to all twelve tests -- and 'RK4
(Adaptive)' in a heading would have sailed through. Headings are
precisely where marketing copy gets title-cased.

mutations.description: a contradicted claim is found but never reported
mutations._note: Everything is examined, nothing is said, the run is green.
A forbidden-phrase list with no phrases forbids nothing.

mutations.description: a stale predicate no longer fails the guard
mutations._note: Each forbidden phrase carries a predicate that re-derives its reason from the code. If the code gains real step adaptation, 'adaptive' becomes accurate and the rule must be revisited -- continuing to forbid a true statement is how guards get deleted.

mutations.description: the fixed-step predicate stops reading the file and just says yes
mutations._note: A check whose evidence has vanished has not passed.

mutations._claimed: 1 failed (after a differently-cased replay was added; NOT caught before)
mutations._note: The escape from the original table. The fix was not to the guard but to the tests: they had only ever been given the casing that already existed in the source.
